senses.text: alphabetical letter The seventh letter of the alphabet: called xaA='N [and xaA (respecting which latter see the letter b )]. It is one of the letters termed mahomuwsap [or non-vocal, i. e. pronounced with the breath only, without the voice]; and of those termed Haloqiy~ap [i. e. faucial, or guttural]: its place of utterance is the same as that of g [which differs from it in being vocal]. (L.) -A2- [As a numeral, it denotes Six hundred. ]

Hence, app.,] xab~a signifies also He alighted and abode in a depressed tract of ground, in order that his place might be unknown, from a motive of niggardliness [ to avoid claims upon his hospitality, thus deceiving passers by ]. [See xaruEa .] ― -b2- (tropical:) Cowardice; and weakness, or feebleness, and languor, or languidness; in a man. (TA.) [See also xariEa .]
(S, K) and ↓ (K) Weak, or infirm; (S, K;) applied to a man: (S:) anything weak; and soft, yielding, flaccid, flabby, lax, or fragile: (O:) also the former, applied to a young camel, weak
; or, as some say, small, that is [or may be ] raised, or lifted: and, applied to a branch, soft, tender, or supple. (TA.)

a subst. from AixotaraEa Al$~aYo'a signifying Airotajalahu [&c.; app. meaning A thing done, or produced, without premeditation; &c.; like bidoEapN from AibotadaEahu , a syn. of AixotaraEahu , q. v.]. (TA.)
: see xariyEN .

Any weak, bending plant, of whatever kind it be: (As, S:) any plant weak, or fragile, ( qaSiyf ,) and sappy, whether it be a tree or a herb: (TA:) a plant weak by reason of its softness, or tenderness, and sappiness. (Sgh.) [See also xariEN .] ― -b2-
Hence, as some say, (TA,) [The ricinus communis; common palma Christi

; or castor-oil-plant; ] a certain plant, (S, Msb, K,) well known, (S,) soft, tender, or pliant, (Msb,) not serving for pasturage, (K,) bearing a berry resembling sparrows' eggs, called Als~imosimu AlhinodiY~u ; accord to Ibn-Jezleh, the best thereof is that called AlbaHoriY~u ; it has the property of loosening phlegm, and it is useful for counteracting the colic and palsy and the [ disease in the face called ] laqowap , the dose extending to a mivoqaAl . (TA.) : see xariEN . ― -b2- Anything that quickly breaks. (TA.) ― -b3- Soft; applied to a lip ( $afap ): (TA:) and pendulous; applied to the lip of a camel. (S, K. *) ― -b4- Applied to a woman, (S, Msb, K, TA,) Youthful, and soft, tender, or delicate: or beautiful: (TA:) or that walks with an affected bending of the body, and with softness, or delicacy: (Msb:) or that affects a bending of the body by reason of softness, or delicacy; (As, S, K;) as also xiriyEapN and ↓ : (Ibn-' Abbád, K:) or (assumed tropical:) vitious
; or an adulteress

; or a fornicatress; (S, K;) but this explanation is disallowed by As: (S:) or (assumed tropical:) that does not repel the hand of a feeler, or toucher; as though she were gentle, or mild, ( tanoxariEu ,) to him; as also with p : or hard, or (assumed tropical:) impudent, not caring for what is said or done, and inordinately brisk, lively, or sprightly: pl. xuruwEN and xaraAy^iEu and xur~aEN . (TA.) Also (assumed tropical:) One who induces, or is an object of, suspicion; because such a person fears, and is therefore as though he were weak. (TA.) ― -b5-
Also, [as a subst.,] A branch; because of its softness, or tenderness, and its bending. (TA.)
a dial. var. of xalaAEapN , which is syn. with daEaArapN [i .e. Vice, or immorality
; or vitious, or immoral, conduct; &c.]. (S.)
A sheep, or goat, having the mark termed xaraEN [q. v.] in the ear. (K.)

: see above, in three places.

: see xaroEabN , in two places. ― -b2- Also A piece of a gourd, and of a cucumber, and of fat; as in the L &c.: in the K written xu*oEuwbapN . (TA.)

Gathered, or plucked, fruits; (S, Mgh, K;) and particularly of the palm-tree: (TA:) and ↓ signifies the same. (Mgh, K, TA. and ↓ The time of the gathering, or plucking, of fruits: (Ks, K:) like HaSaAdN and HiSaAdN [&c.]. (TA.) ― -b2- Also inf. ns. of xarafa in the first of the senses explained above. (K.)

A lamb; syn. HamalN [q. v.]: (S, Msb:) or the male young one of the sheep-kind: or such as has pastured, and become strong: (Lth, K:) younger than the ja*aE : (Lth, TA:) so called because it depastures from this place and this: (Msb, TA: [see 1:]) fem. with p : (K:) pl. Fresh ripe dates, (K, TA,) or fruits [in general], (S, TA,) gathered, or plucked; (S, K, TA;) as also ↓ . (S, TA. See also maxorafN , last sentence. (JK, * K.) ― -b2- And xariqa , aor. , inf. n. xaraqN , said of a gazelle, or young gazelle, (Msb, K, TA,) when hunted, (TA,) or when overtaken by the dog, (IAar,) It was frightened, (Msb, K, TA, [in the CK, Aano yaEoraqa is erroneously put for A^ano yaforaqa ,]) so as to be unable to go away, (Msb,) o

; or he became bereft of his reason or intellect, because of fear, or of shame: (S, Msb, K:) or he was confounded, perplexed, or amazed, [for yatahay~aba in the CK, I read yabohata , as in other copies of the K and in the TA,] opening his eyes, and looking: (K, TA:) and he remained confounded, or perplexed, and unable to see his right course, by reason of anxiety, or of hardship, or distress. senses.text: 1 , aor. , inf.n. xaromN , He perforated, or pierced, it; namely, a thing. (Msb.) [And so xazamahu . (Mgh in art. xzm .)] ― -b2- And He cut it, or cut it off. (Msb.) You say, maA xaramotu minohu $ayoy^FA I did not diminish, and did not cut off, from it, or him, anything. (S.) And maA xarama mina AlHadiyvi HarofFA He did not diminish [ from the narrative, or tradition, a letter, or a word ]. (TA.) And xarama fulaAnFA , (K,) aor, and inf. n. as above, (TA,) He slit the partition between the nostrils of such a one: (K:) or xaromN signifies the mutilating ( qaToE ) of the nose: (JK:) or mutilation ( qaToE ) in the partition between the nostrils and in the naA$irataAni [or two alœ ], or in the extremity of the A^aronabap [or lobule of the nose ]; not amounting to what is termed jadoEN ; (Lth, T

; or in the upper part of the fuwq [app. meaning the front edge of the lobe, which at its termination above forms a crena,] of the ear: (Lth, TA: [see A^axoramu , as relating to the ear:]) accord. to Sh, it is both in the nose and in the ear; but in the nose, it is the mutilation ( qTE ) of the fore part of the nostril of a man, and the A^aronabap [or lobule of the nose ], after the mutilation of the upper part of this, so as to reach the interior of the nose; and the epithet applied to the man is ↓ . (TA.) And xaramahu , inf. n. as above, also signifies He hit, or hurt, his xaworamap [q. v.]. (TA.) You say also, xarama Alxurozapa , (K, TA, in the CK [erroneously] Alxarazapa ,) aor. as above, (K,) and so the inf. n.; (TA;) and ↓ , (K,) inf.n. taxoriymN ; (TA;) He cracked, or tore without s

; or as when one rends two stitch-holes into one ]. (S.) [And xaramahu sayolN app. A torrent cut into it, or trenched it; namely, the ground, or the side of a mountain: see xaromN .] And ↓ [lit. Cutting-off events cut him off ]; meaning (assumed tropical:) he died: like as one says, $aEabatohu $aEuwbu . (TA. [See also

senses.text: 1 , (S, Msb, K,) aor. , (Msb, K,) inf. n. xaloTN , (S, Msb,) He mixed it; mingled it; incorporated, or blended, it; (Msb, K;) or put it together; (Msb;) bigayorihi with another thing; (S, Msb;) inseparably, as in the case of fluids; and separably, as in the case of animals, (Msb, TA,) and grains; (TA;) as also ↓ , (K,) inf. n. taxoliyTN : (TA:) [or the latter relates to many, or several, objects

; or signifies he mixed it much: ] El-Marzookee says that the primary signification of xaloTN is the intermingling of the particles of a thing, one with another. (Msb, TA.) [And hence, (assumed tropical:) He confused, confounded, or disordered, it. ] ― -b2- xalaTa Alqawoma ; and xaliTa : see 3, near the end of the paragraph.

1. ― -b2- [Its inf. n. is pluralized: you say,] jamaEa maAlahu mino taxaAliyTa [ He collected together his property, or camels, &c., from states of confusion ]. (TA.) ― -b3- Alt~axoliyTu fiY AlA^amori signifies The creating confusion, or disorder, ( AlA_ifosaAdu ,) in the affair, or case. (S.) And you say, huwa fiY taxoliyTK fiY A^amorihi [and mino Amrh , He is in a state of confusion, or disorder, in, or with respect to, his affair, or case ]. (TA.) [And xl~T Ealayohi AlA^amori He rendered the affair, or state, or case, confused, or disordered, or perplexed, to him. And xl~T bayona Alqawomi He created confusion, or disorder, or disturbance, among the people, or company of men. ]

3 , inf. n. muxaAlaTapN (S, Mgh, K) and xilaATN , (S, K,) It mixed, mingled, commingled, intermixed, or intermingled, with it; it became incorporated, or blended, with it; syn. maAzajahu ; (Mgh, K;) and xaAmarahu ; (S, A, K, all in art. xmr ;) [as, for instance,] water with milk. (A in art. xmr , and Mgh in the present art.) xilaATN in relation to camels, and men, and beasts, also signifies Their being mixed together. (K.) A poet says, yaxorujona mino buEokuwkapi AlxilaATi [ They come forth from the crowding and dust (of the beasts) occasioned by the being mixed together ]. (Th, TA.) And it is said in a trad., laA xilaATa walaA wiraATa (S, Mgh,) There shall be no putting together what is separate, nor separating what is put together, from fear of the poor-rate: (S:) for the Prophet made it

; or] do not thou mix my A^urojuwzap with thine [ O father of her with the shaggy hair ]; to which El-'Ajjáj replied, AlfijaAju A^awosaEu mino *`lika yaA A@bona A^axiY [ The roads are wider than to require my doing that, O son of my brother ]. (AO, S.) ― -b3- xAlT Al*~iy^obu Alganama [lit. signifying The wolf mixed with the sheep, or goats, ] means (tropical:) the wolf fell upon the sheep, or goats: (K, TA:) the inf. n. is xilaATN . (TA.) ― -b4- xAlThA , (Az, Msb, K,) inf. n. xilaATN and muxaAlaTapN , (Az, Msb,) (tropical:) He had carnal intercourse with her; (Az, Mgh, * Msb, K;) i. e., a man with his wife, (Az, Msb,) or with a woman: (K:) the lawyers say, xAlThA muxaAlaTapa AlAizodiwaAji : (Msb:) Th explains the inf. n. xilaATN by rafavN , q. v. (TA.)
Also, in like manner, with the same inf. ns., (tropical:) a stallion-camel with the female. (Lth, K, TA.) [See also

4.] IAar explains xilaATN in relation to camels as signifying (assumed tropical:) A man's coming to the nightly resting-place of another's camels, and taking thence a male camel, and making him to cover his she-camel without his owner's knowledge. (TA.) ― -b5- xAlThu Als~ahomu (assumed tropical:) [ The arrow penetrated into him ]. (TA.) ― -b6- xAlThu Al$~ayobu [ Hoariness, or whiteness, became intermixed in his hair ]. (S and K in art. wxT ; &c.) ― -b7- xAlThu Ald~aA='u (tropical:) The disease infected, or pervaded, him; [ as though commingling with him; ] syn. xaAmarahu : (Sh, K:) or infected, or pervaded, his inside. (Lth, S.) ― -b8- xaAlaTa qalobahu ham~N EaZiymN (tropical:) [ Great anxiety, or disquietude of mind, infected, or pervaded, his heart ]. (TA.) It is said in a trad., warajaE
; or became intimate with them

; or mixed with them in, or entered with them into, their affairs; syn. daAxalahumo ; as also ↓ , inf. n. xaloTN ; (TA;) and ↓ , like fariHa , is used in a similar manner, in the sense of xaAlaTa : (IAar, TA:) and you say also ↓ biAln~aAsi (assumed tropical:) [ he mixed, or associated, or conversed, with men ]. (TA.) And xaAlaTotu fulaAnFA (assumed tropical:) I mixed with such a one in familiar, or social, intercourse; conversed with him

; or became intimate with him; syn. xaAmarotuhu , (A in art. xmr ,) and EaA$arotuhu . (S, Msb, K, all in art. E$r .) And xAlThu fiY A^amori (assumed tropical:) [ He mixed, or joined, with him in an affair ]. (Mgh.) And hence xAlThu signifies (assumed tropical:) He was, or became, copartner with him; he shared with him. (Mgh.) xaAlaTahumo also signifies xaAlafahumo [evidently a mistranscription, for HaAlafahumo (assumed tropical:) He entered into a confederacy, league, compact, or covenant, with them ]. (TA.) And you say also xAlT AlA^umuwra (assumed tropical:) [ He mixed in, engaged in, or entered into, affairs ]. (S, K.)

(TA.) -A2- AxlT [intrans.] (tropical:) He (a stallion) covered the female. (K.) [This seems to be taken from IF, who, as shown above, makes it syn. with AstxlT . See also
3.] ― -b2- As syn. with AxtlT , see 3, near the end of the paragraph. -A3- Said of a horse, He fell short, or flagged, in his running; as also ↓ . (IDrd, K.)
6 (tropical:) They commingled

; or became mixed, or confounded, together, in war, or battle; as also fY AlHrb ↓ . (TA.) ― -b2- txAlTwA also signifies (assumed tropical:) They commingled, or mixed together, in familiar, or social, intercourse; [ conversed together
; or became intimate, one with another
; or they mixed, one in another's affairs; see 3, near the end;] syn. tEA$rwA . (S, Msb, K, all in art. E$r .)

8 It was, or became, mixed, mingled, commingled, incorporated or blended together, (S, * Msb, K,) or put together. (Msb.) [And hence, (assumed tropical:) It was, or became, confused, confounded, indiscriminate, promiscuous, without order, disordered, or perplexed. ] ― -b2- AxtlT All~ayolu biAlt~uraAbi (assumed tropical:) [ The night became confused, or confounded, with the dust, or earth ]: (AZ, K:) and AlHaAbilu biAln~aAbili (K) (assumed tropical:) the setter of the snare with the shooter of arrows

; or the warp with the woof: (TA:) and AlmaroEaY biAlhamali (assumed tropical:) [ the place of pasturage with the camels left to pasture by themselves ]: (AZ, K:) and AlxaAviru biAlz~ubaAdi (as in some copies of the K and in the TA) (assumed tropical:) the thick milk with the butter that had become bad, or spoiled, in the churning

; or, as some say, with the thin milk; (TA;) or biAlz~ab~aAdi (as in other copies of the K and in the TA) with the herb [ so called ], which, when it falls into the raAy^ib [or milk that is thick, and fit for churning, &c.], is with difficulty separated from it: (TA:) [but see art. zbd :] proverbs, alluding to the dubiousness and confusedness of an affair or a case: (K:) or the first, to the dubiousness of an affair or case; and the second, to its confusedness; and the third is applied when a people's affair or case is confused or perplexed to them; and the last relates to the confusedness of truth with falsity; and to a people whose affair or case is dubious to them, so that they do not decide upon anything. (TA.) ― -b3- [ AxtlT AlZ~alaAmu (assumed tropical:) The darkness, or the beginnin
6. ― -b6- Said of a camel, (tropical:) He became fat; (ISh, K;) his fat and flesh becoming mixed together. (ISh.) ― -b7- Said of a horse: see 4, last sentence.
10 He (a camel) inserted, (AZ,) or directed (K, TA) and inserted, (TA,) his qaDiyb into the HayaA=' , by himself: (AZ, K, TA:) or he leaped the female; syn. qaEaA . (S.) See also

Anything that mixes, mingles, commingles, or becomes incorporated or blended, with a thing; an admixture; (K, TA;) any kind of mixture; as a medicinal mixture; and the like: pl. A^axolaATN . (TA.) ― -b2- A kind of [ mixed ] perfume, (S, * Msb,) well known: (Msb:) pl. as above. (S, Msb.) ― -b3- [Sing. of AxlAT in the term] A^axolaATu AlA_inosaAni The four humours of man, (K, TA,) which are the constituents of his composition; (TA;) namely, Almir~ataAni [ the black bile and the yellow bile ] and Albalogamu [ the phlegm ] and Ald~amu [ the blood ]. (TA in art. mzj .) ― -b4- Mixed dates of various sorts: pl. as above. (K.) ― -b5- (tropical:) A man who mixes with others, and manifests love to them; (TA;) and xiloTapN a woman who does so: (K, * TA:) and the former, (IAar, TA,) or ↓ , (K,) or thi

; or of the lowest or basest or meanest sort, or refuse, or riffraff, thereof; (K, * TA;) as also ↓ , (Ibn-'Abbád, K,) and ↓ , (K,) and ↓ : (Ibn-'Abbád, K:) to these ( lahun~a [in the CK lahum ]) there is no sing.: (K, TA:) but xaliyTN is also a sing., and has pls., as will be seen below. (TA.) ― -b7- (tropical:) Stupid; foolish; having little sense; (IAar, K;) as also ↓ : (IAar, Sgh, K:) pl. of the former A^axolaATN ; (IAar, TA;) with which ↓ is syn. (TA.) ― -b8- A crooked bow, and arrow; (K;) an arrow of which the wood has grown crookedly, and which ceases not to be crooked even if it have been straightened; (S;) as also ↓ , applied to either of these. (K.) And in like manner, (assumed tropical:) a man; he being likened to such an arrow: and (assumed tropical:) a people, or company of me
; fem. with p : see xiloTN , in three places. ― -b2- Also (assumed tropical:) Good in disposition; good-natured. (TA.)
: see xiloTN , in two places: ― -b2- [and see xaliyTN , of which it is a pl.]
: see xiloTN , last sentence but one.

[ A state of mixing, or mingling, together; ] a subst. from AxtlT . (Msb.) ― -b2- [And hence,] (assumed tropical:) Copartnership. (S, Mgh, TA.) You say bayonahumaA xuloTapN (assumed tropical:) Between them two is a copartnership. (Mgh.) [See also what next follows.]
(assumed tropical:) Social, or familiar, intercourse. (S, Msb, TA.) [See also what next precedes.]

[ Mixed; mingled; incorporated, or blended: of the measure faEiylN in the sense of the measure mafoEuwlN ; like qatiylN &c. And hence,] (K,) or EalafN xaliyTN , (S, TA,) [ The kind of trefoil called ] qat~ and cut straw (S, TA) mixed together: (TA:) or clay mixed with cut straw: (K, TA:) or with qat~ . (K.)
Also, (K,) or labanN xaliyTN , (TA,) Sweet milk mixed with sour or such as bites the tongue. (K, TA.)

Also, (K,) or samonN xaliyTN , (TA,) Clarified butter in which are fat and flesh-meat. (K, TA.) [Hence also,] it is said in a trad. respecting [the beverage called] nabiy* , (TA,) nuhiYa Eani AlxaliyTayoni (S, K) fiY AlA^anobi*api (S) or A^ano yunoba*aA (K) [ Two sorts of things mixed together are forbidden in the beverages of the kind called nby* , or that nby* should be made of them ]; i. e. it is forbidden to mix together [for making nby* ] two sorts of things; (S, TA;) meaning dried dates and raisins; (S, Mgh, K;) or fresh grapes and fresh ripe dates; (S;) or dried dates and full-grown unripe dates, (T, Mgh, K,) thoroughly cooked by fire; (Mgh;) or fresh grapes and raisins; (T, K;) and the like; because such nby* quickly alters, and becomes intoxicating: (K:) and some hold that nby* so
; or becomes intimate with them

; or mixes with them in, or enters with them into, their affairs; syn. with ↓ ; (S, K;) like as nadiymN is syn. with munaAdimN , and jaliysN with mujaAlisN : (S:) pl. xulaTaA='u (S, Msb, K) and xuluTN : (S, K:) it sometimes has these pls., but is itself both sing. and pl.: (S, TA:) and as a pl. signifies (assumed tropical:) a people, or company of men, whose affair, or case, or state, is one: (K, TA:) it occurs frequently in the poems of the Arabs because they used to assemble in the days of the fresh herbage, sundry tribes of them congregating in one place, and familiar intercourse took place between them, and when they separated and returned to their homes, it grieved them: (S, TA:) or, accord. to some, it relates only to partnership: (TA:) it signifies (assumed tropical:) a partner, cop
(tropical:) Stupidity; foolishness; paucity of sense. (IAar, K.)
Camel's milk milked upon that of sheep or goats: or sheep's milk upon that of goats: and the reverse. (K.)
: see xiloTN : ― -b2- and see what next follows, in two places.

: see xiloTN . ― -b2- waqaEuwA fiY xul~ayoTaY , (S, K,) and ↓ , (K,) (assumed tropical:) They fell into a state of confusion: (K:) their affair, or case, became confused, or perplexed, ( AixotalaTa ,) to them. (S.) And ↓ (assumed tropical:) [ We were in a state of confusion ]: cited by Az, from an Arab of the desert. (TA.) 2.] ― -b2- maAluhumo xil~iyTaY~N [in the CK mAlahumo ] Their possessions, or camels &c., are mixed together. (K, * TA.)
: see xul~ayoTaY .
(tropical:) [ More insinuating than fever ]; a saying of the Arabs; meaning that it manifests an affection for a person by its access to him, like the lover and blandisher. (TA.)

(assumed tropical:) One who renders things confused, or dubious, to the hearers and beholders. (TA.) ― -b2- (assumed tropical:) One who mixes in, or enters into, ( yuxaAliTu ,) affairs, (S, K, TA,) and relinquishes them; (TA; [but this addition seems rather to apply to mizoyalN in what follows;]) as also ↓ : (K:) or this latter signifies (assumed tropical:) one who mixes much with men. (Sgh, TA.) [See also xaliyTN .] You say, huwa mixolaTN mizoyalN (assumed tropical:) [ He is one who mixes in, or enters into, affairs; (and, accord. to an explanation of mizoyalN in the TA, in art. zyl , on the authority of IAth,) one who is vehement in altercation, or litigation, relinquishing one plea, or argument, and taking to another ]; like as you say, huwa raAtiqN faAtiqN . (S, K.)
: see mixolaTN .
(tropical:) Infected, corrupted, disordered, or confused, in his intellect; as also ↓ : (TA:) or mad; insane
; or affected by diabolical possession. (TA in art. lbs .)
: see xaliyTN .
: see muxaAlaTN . ― -b2- Also (tropical:) A camel that has become fat, so that the fat is mixed with the flesh: fem. with p , applied to a she-camel. (ISh, K.)

senses.text: 1 , (S, Mgh, Msb,) aor. , (TA,) inf. n. xaloEN , (S, Mgh, Msb, K,) He pulled it off; syn. nazaEahu ; (Mgh, Msb;) or stripped it off

; or took it off; (TA;) or put it, or threw it, or cast it, off from him; (IAth;) namely, his garment, (S, IAth, Mgh, Msb,) Eano badanihi from his body; (Mgh;) and his sandal, (S, Mgh, Msb,) Eano rijolihi from his foot; (Mgh;) &c.; (Msb, TA;) [as also ↓ , as appears from its being said that] AixotilaAEN is syn. with xaloEN : (TA:) accord. to some, xaloEN is syn. with nazoEN ; but accord. to Lth, (TA,) the former is like the latter, except that the former is a somewhat leisurely action. (K, TA.) The phrase in the Kur [xx. 12], faA@xolaEo naEolayoka is said to be used in its proper sense, [ And do thou pull off, or put off, thy sandals, ] because his sandals were of the skin of a dead ass: or, as the Soofees say, it is a command to stay; like as you say to him whom you desire to stay, “ Pull

; or] he released him from his shackles: and in like manner, xalaEa daAb~atahu , and ↓ , he released his beast from its shackles. (TA.) ― -b11- xalaEa yadFA mino TaAEapK (tropical:) He [ threw off his allegiance, or] forsook obedience to his Sultán, and acted in a wrongful and evil manner towards him: (TA:) obedience being likened to a garment which a man puts off, or throws off, from him. (Mgh.) ― -b13- [In like manner you say,] xalaEotu AlwaAliY Eano Eamalihi (tropical:) I removed t
; or deposed him. (Msb.) And xuliEa AlwaAliY (tropical:) [ The ruler, or governor, or the like, was divested of his authority

; or was deposed; (S, TA;) and so AlEaAmilu [ the agent, or the exactor of the poor-rates ]; and Alxaliyfapu [ the Khaleefeh ]. (TA.) And xalaEa qaAy^idahu (tropical:) [ He divested his leader of his authority
; or removed him from his office

; or dismissed him ]. (S, TA.) But IF says, This is scarcely, or never, said, except of an inferior who forsakes, or relinquishes, his superior; so that [ xalaEahu signifies, in a case of this kind, (tropical:) He threw off his allegiance to him

; or forsook obedience to him; like another phrase, mentioned above; and] one does not say, [or seldom says,] xalaEa AlA^amiyru waAliyahu EalaY baladi ka*aA [as meaning (assumed tropical:) The prince deposed his ruler over such a province, or the like ]; but only, [or rather,] Eazalahu . (TA.) ― -b14- xalaEa A@moraA^atahu , (Az, S, Mgh, Msb,) inf. n. xuloEN , with damm, (S, K, *) or this is a simple subst., (Az, Mgh, Msb,) and the inf. n. is xaloEN , (Az, Msb, TA,) and some add xilaAEN ; (TA;) and ↓ , (Az, TA,) inf. n. muxaAlaEapN ; (K;) [and xilaAEN seems to be another inf. n. of this latter verb, rather than of the former;] (tropical:) He divorced his wife (Az, Mgh, Msb, K) for a ransom given by her, (Msb,) or for her property given by her as a ransom to release herself from him, (Az, Mg
; or the like: see xalaAEapN , below; and see xaliyEN .] -A3- xuliEa He became affected with what is termed xaAliEN , i. e., a twisting of the EuroquwbN [or hock-tendon ]. (K.)

Flesh-meat cooked with seeds that are used for seasoning, then put into a receptacle of skin, (S, K, *) which is called qarofN : (S:) or flesh-meat cut into strips or oblong pieces, and dried, or salted, and dried in the sun, roasted, (K, TA,) and, as Lth says, (TA,) put into a receptacle with its melted grease: (K, * TA:) or flesh-meat having its bones pulled out, then cooked, and seasoned with seeds, and put into a skin, and used as provision for travelling: (Z, TA:) and ↓ , also, signifies flesh-meat of which the bones have been pulled out, and which is seasoned with seeds, and laid up ( yurofaEu ) [ for future use ]: (TA:) and ↓ , flesh-meat which is boiled in vinegar, and then carried in journeys. (TA.) -A2- A state of dislocation of the joint, of the arm or hand, or of the leg or foo

[accord. to the S, and app. accord. to the K, and inf. n., (see xalaEa A@moraA^atahu ,) or] a simple subst., signifying (tropical:) The act of divorcing a wife (Az, Mgh, Msb) for a ransom given by her, (Msb,) or for her property given by her as a ransom to release her from her husband, (Az, Mgh, TA,) or for a gift, or a compensation, from her

; or from another: (K: see 1:) IAth says that it annuls the return to the wife unless by means of a new contract: accord. to EshSháfi'ee, there is a difference of opinion respecting it; whether it be an annulment of the marriage, or a divorcement: [if the latter, it is not irrevocable unless preceded by two divorcements:] sometimes it is called by the latter term. A state of divorcement [for a ransom given by the wife, or for her property given by her as a ransom to release her from her husband, or] for a gift, or a compensation, from the wife, (S, * K,) or from another. (K.) [See 8: and see also xuloEN .] You say, waqaEato bayonahumaA AlxuloEapu [ Divorcement, or] separation, [ for a ransom, &c. or] for [ a gift, or] a compensation, took place between them two. (TK.) -A2- (assumed tropical:) The best, or choice part, of property, or of camels or the like; (Aboo-Sa'eed, S Sgh, K;) so called because it takes away the heart of him who looks at it; (Aboo-Sa'eed;) as also ↓ . (Aboo-Sa'eed, Sgh, K.) -A3- (assumed tropical:) Weakness in a man. (TA.)

Any garment which one pulls off, or takes off, from himself: (TA:) and particularly, (TA,) a garment which is bestowed upon a man, [generally meaning a robe of honour, ] (K, * TA,) whether it be put upon him or not: (TA:) or a gift, or free gift, [of any kind,] which a man bestows upon another: (Msb:) or a sewed garment: (KL:) pl. xilaEN . (Msb, TA.) You say, xalaEa Ealayohi xiloEapF [explained above]: see 1, near the beginning. (S, TA.) ― -b2- See also xuloEapN .
, with damm, One who sells [ cast-off or] old garments. (Ibn-Nuktah, TA.)
, with kesr to the x , and with the l quiescent, One who sells the garments bestowed by kings. (TA.)

(assumed tropical:) An affection resembling what is termed xabalN [q. v.], (K, TA,) and insanity, or diabolical possession, (TA,) which befalls a man: (K, TA:) or weakness, and fear or fright: (TA:) and ↓ and ↓ [in like manner] signify (tropical:) fear, or fright, affecting the heart, (S, K, TA,) occasioning evil imagination, and weakness, (TA.) as though it were a touch of insanity, or of diabolical possession, (S, K, TA,) in a man, and in the heart. (S.)
Pulled off; stripped, or taken, off; put, or thrown, or cast, off; i. q. ↓ ; applied [to a garment, and a sandal, or the like, or], accord. to some, to anything. (TA.) ― -b2- [

(TA.) ― -b3- See also xaloEN . ― -b4- (assumed tropical:) A person whose property is won from him in a game of hazard; as also ↓ . (L.) ― -b5- xaliyEu AlEi*aAri (assumed tropical:) (assumed tropical:) A man who does and says what he pleases; not caring, nor fearing God nor the blame of men; like the beast that has no halter on its head. (Har p.

676.) Also applied to a woman in a state of estrangement [from her husband; lit., Having her headstall, or halter, pulled off, or thrown off; she being likened to a mare; meaning, (assumed tropical:) (assumed tropical:) without restraint ]; having none to command or forbid her: [see 1:] incorrectly written xaliyEapu AlEi*aAri ; for xlyE is here of the measure faEiylN in the sense of the measure mafoEuwlN : or you say xaliyfapN without mentioning the E*Ar , from xalaEapN , like ZariyfapN and laTiyfapN [from ZaraAfapN and laTaAfapN ]. (Mgh.) [See also xaAliEN .] ― -b6- xaliyEN is also applied to a Khaleefeh, and a prince or the like, meaning (tropical:) Divested of his authority; removed from his office; deposed; (L;) as also ↓ : and it is a strange thing, noticed by Dmr and others, that eve
; or because his family have cast him off, and declared themselves clear of him; (Mgh;) or because he has cast off his kinsfolk, and they have declared themselves clear of him

; or because he is divested of religion and shame; (TA;) fem. with p : (K: [indicating that it is a part. n. of xaluEa ; not of the measure faEiylN in the sense of the measure mafoEuwlN , as is implied by some portions of the explanations here given:]) (assumed tropical:) bad, evil, wicked, or mischievous: (TA:) (tropical:) [ vitious, or immoral: (see xalaAEapN , whence it is derived:)] (assumed tropical:) notorious for drinking and play: (TA:) [in the present day commonly used in this sense; and as signifying (assumed tropical:) waggish

; or a way: ] (assumed tropical:) a player, with another, at a game of hazard, or for stakes laid by both of them to be taken by the winner; (IDrd, K;) as also ↓ ; because the best, or choice part, of his property ( xuloEatuhu ) is [often] won from him: (S:) (assumed tropical:) one who applies himself constantly to games of that kind: (TA:) and ↓ signifies (tropical:) a player at games of that kind, who has had the punishment termed Had~N inflicted upon him, and is always overcome in such games, or who is fortunate, and always overcomes in such games. (K, accord. to different copies; in some of which we read AlmuqaAmiru AlmaHoduwdu Al~a*iY yuqomaru A^abadFA ; and in others, AlmqASr Almajoduwdu Al*Y yaqomuru AbdA .) ― -b8- (assumed tropical:) A hunter, fowler, or fisherman; (S, Sgh, K;) so
: [see xaluEa :] it is syn. with daEaArapN [i. e. (tropical:) Vice, or immorality
; or vitious, or immoral, conduct; &c.]; as also xaraAEapN , a dial. var. thereof; (S in art. xrE ;) and ↓ signifies the same. (TA.)
: see what next precedes.

[(assumed tropical:) A horse throwing off his headstall, or halter, and wandering about at random. ― -b2- And hence, (assumed tropical:) (assumed tropical:) A man throwing off from himself restraint, and acting in a wrongful and an evil manner towards others, with none to repress him. ; or one whose mustache has grown forth, but not his beard. (TA.) ― -b4- xaAliEN (assumed tropical:) A kid. (TA.) (K.) ― -b6- ruTabN xaAliEN Dates that are all ripe, or ripe throughout, or soft; syn. munosabitN ; (S, K;) because their skins strip off by reason of their succulency: (TA:) and busorapN xaAliEN , (K, TA,) and xaAliEapN , (TA,) a date that has become wholly fit to be eaten. (K, * TA.) [See b

: see xaloEN . ― -b2- It also signifies habiyd [i. e. Colocynth, or its pulp, or seed, ] when it is cooked until its samon [or decocted juice ] comes forth, whereupon it is cleared, and put aside; and bruised dates of which the stones have been taken out are put upon it, and flour, and it is stirred about and beaten until it becomes mixed; then it is left, and put down; and when it becomes cold, its smn is restored to it: or, as some say, colocynth ( HanoZal ) bruised, moistened with something to sweeten it, and then eaten; also called mubas~alN . (TA.) [See habiydN .] -A2- See also xulaAEN : -A3- and xaliyEN , in four places. -A4- Also Stupid; (K;) applied to a man. (TA.) -A5- And A skilful guide. (Sgh, K.)
: see xulaAEN : -A2- and see xaliyEN , in two places, near the end. ― -b2- Also (assumed tropical:) A weak man. (TA.) [See also muxal~aEN .]

A man (S) having the buttocks apart, or parted. (S, K.) ― -b2- And muxal~aEN A weak, and soft, or flabby, man. (Lth, K.) [See also xayolaEN .] ― -b3- (tropical:) A man (TA) in whom is what resembles a loss of reason, or a touch of insanity or of diabolical possession: (K, * TA:) and (tropical:) a man insane, or possessed by a jinnee. (TA.)
: see xaliyEN , in four places. ― -b2- rajulN maxoluwEu Alfuw^aAdi (tropical:) A man frightened, or terrified; as though his heart were removed from its place. (TA.)
: see xaliyEN , in the latter part of the paragraph.

(tropical:) A woman divorced from her husband for a gift, or a compensation, from him, (S, K,) or from another: (K:) [see 8:] and [the pl.] muxotaliEaAtN [is explained as signifying] (tropical:) women who incite, urge, or induce, their husbands to divorce them for a gift, or a compensation, without any injurious conduct from the latter. senses.text: 1 , aor. , inf. n. xalofN , He came after, followed, succeeded, or remained after, another, or another that had perished or died. (TA.)
Hence, in the Kur [vii.
168 and xix. 60], faxalafa mino baEodihimo xalofN (TA) And there hath succeeded them, or come after them, [ a posterity, or] an evil posterity. (Bd in xix.

60.) And xalafahu He came after him, (S, A in art. dbr , Mgh, Msb, TA,) or behind him, (A ubi suprà, Mgh,) or following him nearly; (A ubi suprà;) inf. n. as above, (Mgh, TA,) and xilofapN also: (Mgh:) or he remained after him: (K:) and ↓ likewise signifies [the same as jA=' xalofahu ; an inf. n. of xaAlafa being thus used as an adv. n.; i. e.] he came after him. (TA.) You say also, xalafa All~ayolu Aln~ahaAra , inf. n. xalofN and xilofapN , The night followed, or came after, the day. (MA.) ― -b2- [Hence,] xalafotuhu , [aor. as above,] inf. n. xalofN , [perhaps a mistranscription for xalafa ,] I was, after him, a substitute for him: (TA:) [ I supplied his place: and I superseded him. ] And xalafahu , (aor. as above, TA,) inf. n. xilaAfapN (S, Mgh, Msb, K, TA) and xalafN (TA) and xil~iyqaY

; or became substituted for other fruit. (JK, * K,* TA. [In the CK, SaAra xalofFA is erroneously put for SaArato xalafFA .]) And xalafa fulaAnN EalaY fulaAnapa , inf. n. xilaAfapN , [like Eaqaba EalayohaA ,] Such a man took as his wife such a woman after another husband [and thus supplied his place]. (Z, TA.) ― -b3- xalafa ulaAnFA , (aor. , TA,) He took, or seized, such a one from behind him; (JK, * K;) as also ↓ . (TA.) And hence, (TA,) xalafa lahu biAls~ayofi (JK, TA) He came to him from behind him, and smote his neck, or struck off his head, with the sword. (TA.) ― -b4- xalafa fulaAnN biEaqibiY [is explained as meaning] Such a one stayed, or abode, after me. (Msb in art. Eqb ) [But] ― -b5- xalafa biEaqabi fulaAnK is said by some to mean A_ilaY ↓ A^aholihi [q. v.]: accord. to As, however

Hence, app.,] one says also, A_in~a A@moraA^apa fulaAnK taxolufu zawojahaA biAln~izaAEi A_ilaY gayorihi A_i*aA gaAba EanohaA [ Verily the wife of such a one is unfaithful to her husband by yearning towards another when he is absent from her: or deceives her husband behind his back by yearning towards another; for it is implied, by an ex. given, that A*A gAb EnhA is added by way of explanation]. (TA.) xalafahu also signifies He spoke of him, or mentioned him, [ behind his back, or] when he was not present: so in the phrase, xalafahu bixayorK or bi$ar~K [ He spoke of him behind his back well or ill ]. (TA.) And one says, yaxolufu Aln~aAsa mino waraAy^ihimo [meaning He defames men behind their backs ]: the action signified hereby is like giybapN , and may be [ by making signs ] with the side

411.) ― -b10- And He (a man, Sgh) ascended a mountain. (Sgh, K.) -A2- See also 2, first sentence. -A3- xalafa , (S, Msb, K, &c.,) aor. xuluwfN , (Lh, Msb, TA, and Ham p. 679,) [inf. n. xuluwfN ,] said of the taste of water, It was, or became, different from, or contrary to, what it was thought to be: and [hence,] it was, or became, altered [ for the worse ]: (Ham ubi suprà:) [and] said of milk, (S, K,) and of food, (Lh, S, Msb, K,) and the like, (Lh, TA,) and some say xalufa , (TA,) aor. , inf. n. xuluwfN , (Lh, TA,) of both verbs, (TA,) it was, or became, altered [ for the worse ] (Lh, S, Msb, K) in taste, or in odour; (S, Msb, K;) as also ↓ : or, said of milk, the first signifies it became bad from being long kept

; or, as in the A, (tropical:) what was good thereof became mixed ( xulifa , i. e. xuliTa ,) with other milk: and ↓ , said of milk, signifies also it was, or became, sour: (TA:) and the first, said of [the beverage called] nabiy* , it became bad. (K.)

Also, inf. n. xuluwfN (S, Mgh, Msb, K) and xuluwfapN (K) and xilofapN , (L, TA,) said of the mouth (S, Mgh, Msb, K) of a person fasting, (S, Msb, K,) It was, or became, altered [ for the worse ] in odour; (S, Mgh, Msb, K;) as also ↓ . (S, Msb, K.) It is said in a trad. that the xuluwf of the mouth of one who is fasting is sweeter in the estimation of God than the odour of musk: or, accord. to some of the lawyers and of the relaters of traditions, xaluwf ; but [SM says,] I think this to be a mistake, as several affirm it to be, while others say that it is of a bad dial. : accord. to one reading, it is xilofap . (TA.) ― -b2- [Hence,] xalafa Eano xuluqi A^abiyhi , (K,) aor. , inf. n. xuluwfN , (TA,) (assumed tropical:) He was, or became, altered [ for the worse ] from the natural disposition

; or xalofa , aor. , inf. n. xalaAfapN and xuluwfN ; (TA;) (assumed tropical:) He (a man) was, or became, bad, or corrupt. (ISk, S, K, TA.) ― -b4- And xalafa , (K) inf. n. xalaAfapN (IAth, K) and xuluwfN , (K,) (assumed tropical:) He (a man) was, or became, stupid, or foolish

2 , (Msb,) and xl~fhu waraA='ahu , (S, TA,) inf. n. taxoliyfN , (TA,) He left him behind him; (Msb;) namely, a man: (S, Msb, TA:) and ↓ [signifies the same: or] he made him to be behind him; as also ↓ [q.v.], and ↓ : (TA:) [whence the saying,] A^aloHaHotu EalaY fulaAnK ↓ i. e. [ I pressed upon such a one in following ] until I made him to be behind me. (ISk, TA.) You say also, xal~afahumo , inf. n. as above, meaning He was, or became, or went, before them; and left them behind him. (TA.) And xl~fwA A^avoqAlahum , inf. n. as above, They left their loads, or baggage &c., behind their backs; (O, K;) when they went away to draw water. (TA.) ― -b2- [Hence,] xl~fhu He made him, or appointed him, his xaliyfap [i. e. successor, or vice-agent, &c.]; (K;) and so ↓ . (S, Msb, K.) So in the Kur [xxiv.
3 , (Mgh, Msb, TA,) inf. n. xilaAfN (S, Mgh, Msb, K, TA) and muxaAlafapN , (S, Msb, K, TA,) He [or it ] disagreed with, or differed from, him [or it ]

; or he dissented from him; (Mgh, Msb;) contr. of waAfaqahu ; fiY ka*aA [ in, or in respect of, such a thing ]: (Mgh:) and he, or it, was contrary, opposed, or repugnant, to him, or it: (TA:) [and he acted contrarily, contrariously, adversely, or in opposition, to him, or it; he, or it, contravened, or opposed, him, or it: ] and he [or it ] contradicted him [or it ]. (M in art. nqD .) It is said in a prov., A_in~amaA A^anota xilaAfa AlD~abuEi Alr~aAkiba , i. e. tuxaAlifu xilaAfa AlD~abuEi [ Verily thou art one who acts with the contrariousness of the hyena towards the rider ]: for the hyena [attacks a man on foot, but], when it sees the rider, flees from him. (IAar, TA.) You say also, xaAlafaniY Eano ka*aA He turned away from such a thing [ in opposition to me, or] when I betook myself to

; or betook himself to the thing after he had forbidden him it. (TA.) And hence, (Mgh,) huwa yuxaAlifu A_ilaY A@moraA^api fulaAnK , (S, Mgh, *) or A_ilaY fulaAnapa , (O, L, TA,) in the K erroneously, hw yxAlf fulaAnapa , (TA,) He comes to the wife of such a one when he [the latter] is absent from her, (S,) or to such a woman when her husband is absent from her: (Mgh, * O, L, K, TA:) and xAlfhu A_ilaY A^aholihi [ he came to his (another's) wife in his (the husband's) absence]: see 1, in the former half of the paragraph. (Az, TA.) And xAlfhu A_ilayohimo He watched to see him, and, when he was absent from them, namely, his family, he went in to them: (Jm, O, TA:) and, accord. to AZ, fulaAnN SaAHibahu ↓ Such a one watched to see his companion, and, when he was absent, he came, and went in to h
108.) [And xAlf bayona Al$~ayoy^ayoni He put, or placed, the two things contrariwise

senses.text: 1 signifies The act of measuring
; or determining the measure, proportion, or the like, of a thing; and the making a thing by measure, or according to the measure of another thing

; or proportioning a thing to another thing; syn. taqodiyrN : (S, Msb, K, TA, and Bd in ii. 19:) this is the primary meaning. (Msb, TA, and Bd ubi suprà.) You say, xalaqa AlA^adiymi , (S, Msb, K,) aor. , (S, TA,) inf. n. xaloqN (JK, S, Msb, K) and xaloqapN , (K,) He measured, or proportioned, ( qad~ara ,) the hide, and sewed it: (K:) or he measured, or proportioned, ( qd~r ,) the hide, (JK, S, Msb, K,) limaA yuriydu [ for, or to, that which he desired to make of it], (JK, * TA,) or lils~iqaA='i [ for, or to, the skin for water or milk that he desired to make], (Msb,) before cutting it; (S, K, TA;) he measured it ( qaAsahu ) to cut from it a water-bag, or a water-skin, or a boot: (TA:) and in like manner, xalaqa Aln~iTaEa he measured, &c., the nTE [q. v.]: when one cuts it, one says, faraAh

[ xalaA AlmakaAnu mina Aln~aAsu wa AlmaA='i waAlkalaA^ means The place was, or became, devoid, or destitute, of human beings and water and herbage or pasturage; without human beings &c.] Of a place of alighting or abode, you say, xalaA mino A^aholihi and ↓ [ It was, or became, devoid, or destitute, of its occupants ]. (Msb.) And of a vessel, xalaA mim~aA fiyhi It was, or became, empty of what was in it. (Mgh.) And xalawotu Eani AlT~aEaAmi (S) I b

45 and lxi. 14], mano A^anoSaAriY A_ilaY A@ll~`hu . (S.) A man says to another man, Auxolu maEiY Hat~aY A^ukal~imaka , i. e. Be [or come ] thou alone with me [ that I may speak to thee in private]. (TA.) And one says, xalaA bizawojatihi , inf. n. xalowapN , [but see what is said of this noun above,] He was, or became, alone with his wife: but [properly speaking, according to the law,] the term xalowapN [or xalowapN SaHiyHapN , in this case,] is not used unless it be with the enjoyment of AlmufaAxa*ap , [see

3 in art. fx* ,] and then it has an effect upon the circumstances of the marriage [by its rendering obligatory the payment of the dowry, though consummation has not taken place]: if with consummation, the act is termed duxuwlN . (Msb.) You say also, ↓ A^amoraka and biA^amorika Be thou alone in thine affair, with none to take part with thee in it; confine thyself to it exclusively of other things. (TA. [See also

5.]) And A_ilayoka ↓ Keep thou to thine affair, and be alone in it, with none to take part with thee therein. (JK.) And AlbukaA='u ↓ [app. for biAlbukaA='i ] He was, or became, alone in weeping, with none to participate with him in it. (TA.) [And xalaA liloA^amori : see

Such a one fed upon milk and flesh-meat alone; (JK;) or such a one ate not, nor mixed, anything with milk and flesh-meat: and Kináneh and Keys say ↓ . (Lh, JK, * TA.) [And it seems to be indicated in the T that xalawoA signifies They selected a she-camel for a xaliy~ap , q. v.: or i. q. taxal~awoA bixalay~ipK : see
5.] ― -b3- xalaA also ssignifies He devoted himself to religious services or exercises [app. in solitude, or seclusion, or in a xalowap

; or because the doing so involves abstraction from other affairs]. (TA. [See also 5; and see musotaxolK .]) ― -b4- And xalaA bihi [sometimes] signifies (tropical:) He mocked at, scoffed at, laughed at, derided, or ridiculed, him: (Lh, S, Z, K, TA:) said by Az to be strange, and not known by him or any other authority than that of Lh: (TA:) from the saying, xalaA fulaAnN biEiroDi fulaAnK yaEobavu bihi [ Such a one occupied himself alone with the honour, or reputation, of such a one, making sport with it ]. (Ksh in ii.

13.) And i. q. xaAdaEahu (tropical:) [ He deceived, deluded, beguiled, circumvented, or outwitted, him; &c.: or he strove to do so ]: (TA:) as also ↓ , (JK, and K in art. xlY ,) inf. n. muxaAlaApN . (JK.) ― -b5- And xalaA Ealayohi He relied upon him; [as though he betook himself to him alone;] syn. AiEotamada . (TA.) ― -b6- And xalaA , (JK, K,) inf. n. xuluw~N , (TA,) or xalaA='N , (JK,) said of a man (JK) and of a thing, (JK, TA,) He, or it, went, went away, or passed away. (JK, K.)

Hence, (TA,) wa A_ino mino A^um~apKA_il~aA xalaA fiyhaA na*iyrN , in the Kur [xxxv. 22], means [ And there is not any people but a warner ] hath gone, and hath been sent, among them. (S, TA.) [Hence also xalaA explained above as meaning He died. ] And xalaA minohaA [an elliptical phrase] She became old; the greater part of her life passed. (TA from a trad.) And xalaAka *am~N [for xalaA Eanoka *am~N ] Blame passed away from thee
2 , inf. n. taxoliyapN , [ He left a place, &c., empty, vacant, void, devoid, destitute, or unoccupied. ]

Hence, xl~Y makaAnahu [ He left his place vacant; ] meaning (tropical:) he died: (TA, and so in Ham p. 478:) a meaning assigned in the K to ↓ makaAnuhu , and by IAar to xalaA alone, without tesh-deed; but when mkAnh is added, it is with teshdeed. (TA.) And (assumed tropical:) He went his way. (Ham p.

379.) And xl~Y sabiylahu [ He left his way free, or open, to him ]. (S, TA.) And xl~Y bayonahumaA [ He left the way, or space, free between them two; meaning he left them two free, each to do to the other as he pleased ]. (TA.) [And xl~Y bayonahu wabayona ka*aA He left him free access to such a thing. ] And xl~Y bayonahu wa bayona nafosihi He left him, or it, alone; syn. A^ahomalahu . (S and O and K in art. hml .) [And xl~Ahu wafulaAnFA He left him to do as he pleased with such a one. ] And xl~Y AlA^amora He left, left alone, or let alone, the thing, or affair; as also ↓ minohu and Eanohu ; and ↓ , (K, TA,) inf. n. xilaA='N . 123.)
